channel.title: Texas Landman & Title Tech
channel.description: Primary-source benchmarks, unit economics, learning-curve indices, Texas mineral case law, and RRC regulatory intelligence for working landmen, title examiners, brokerages, and E&P land departments.

item.title: Clifton v. Johnson & Fasken v. Puig (Tex. 2026): Why 1950s Double-Fraction Deeds and Postproduction Clauses Break Naive AI Title Prompts
item.description: For the first time since Van Dyke v. Navigator Group, the Texas Supreme Court held that four-corners deed text rebutted the 1/8 estate-misconception presumption — fixing a 1951 conveyance at 1/128 rather than 1/16. Weeks later, Fasken Oil & Ranch v. Puig proved "free of cost forever" still bears postproduction deductions.

item.title: Texas RRC Crosses 100.2 Million Digitized Files, Ends Paper P-5/PR Filings on LoneSTAR, and Opens SB 1150 Inactive-Well Rulemaking
item.description: What the Railroad Commission's 2026 digital overhaul, record 2,022 orphan-well pluggings, and November 2026 Chapter 3 inactive-well hearings mean for Held-by-Production (HBP) lease checks and wellborecurative work.

item.title: The 2026 Texas Courthouse Record Cost Fact Sheet: TexasFile vs. CourthouseDirect vs. CountyRecords.com, SB 16 Clerk Rules, and the Rural Gap
item.description: Exact 2026 per-page, per-document, preview, and county-plant fee schedules across Texas's Big Three portals — plus how "view-before-buy" discipline cuts raw deed spend by 65% and where physical courthouse vaults still win.

item.title: Inside the Fall 2026 AI Title Wave: Why Three-Model Verification & Deterministic BigInt Math Beat Single-Model Chatbots
item.description: Evaluating the rapid cluster of 2026 launches — TitleDesk, Artificial Landman, Enverus Runsheet Assistant, Energy Domain MCP, RecordsOnline AI Suite, and Quorum Data Extraction — on verification rigor.

item.title: Browser Title Runs vs. Local Desktop Workstation: A Practical Deployment Guide for Solo Landmen, Brokerages, and E&P Teams
item.description: When to fire a zero-setup $249 four-sheet workbook run on Artificial Landman or TitleDesk Web — and when to live inside the $199/mo TitleDesk Desktop Agent for multi-tract units, offline TIFF OCR, and custom client folder trees.
